page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. A verse quotation set in italic and indented, with its reference "Verf. 8." above it, sits mid-page. No marginal notes. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.l: quin exigat profundam debellatorum subjectionem & prostrationem, quod generosis animis durum telum est,
& cum vilissimâ rigidâque servitute conjunctum. Ita
Deum non metuentes judicem, nec debitâ venera-
tione colentes, ex lege talionis, cogerentur terribilis &
superbissimæ gentis terrores & exactiones experiri.
§. 2. Adjungit & aliud malum, judicium ejus & prolatio
ejus exhibit. De vocibus, & phrasi confer dicta
verf. 1. & 4. Symmachus apud Theodoritum vertit ἀυτὸς ἑαυτὸν δοξάσει (lege δικάσει)
καὶ δόγμα τὸ ἑαυτῆ ἐ-πεξελεύσεται[?] ut prolationem exponat per dogma, de-
cretum, aut legem positivam ex placito ejus profluen-
tem. Hæc respiciunt potestatem utramque cum judicia-
riam, tum legislatoriam: fore enim denunciat Deus, ut
gentis istius judicio in foro standum sit cadendumve
aliis gentibus: & ut ab eâ leges & statuta exeant, quibus
obtemperandum sit. Quod sanè grave foret
Judæis, quorum causæ ita negligerentur: quique forte
legibus urgerentur ad falsorum numinum cultum: ita, qui
legem Dei neglexerunt, & judicium corruperunt,
judicandi potestate ad justorum oppressionem abusi, adigerentur
ad leges ab iis recipiendas, & judices, qui religioni
Judaicæ parum essent favent[?]es.
Verf. 8.

page.notes: Greek line after "dicta verf. 1. & 4." is transcribed from the scan; the accents and the hyphen in ἐ-πεξελεύσεται are uncertain and marked [?]. "venient" in the verse is partly obscured and marked [?]. "favent-es" line-break: the word is printed "favent es" and is read as faventes. The last line of §. 1 is cut off at the foot of the page and continues on the next page; the catchword "præ" carries it on.
